title: Guidelines for Neuroprognostication in Critically ill Adults with Acute Ischemic Stroke

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 1
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that prognostication should be multimodal, with consideration of the complete clinical condition, and never based on a single variable. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 2
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that the assessment of neurological prognosis be performed in the absence of potential confounders of the neurological exam. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 3
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that preexisting functional impairment and comorbidities be considered when formulating a prognosis. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 4
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that counseling of critically ill patients with AIS expected to survive the index hospital admission, and/or their surrogates, include discussion of long-term functional outcomes. Discussion should not focus on day-to-day changes and in-hospital outcomes alone. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 5
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that acceptable outcomes for individual patients serve as the basis for prognostication and shared decision-making. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 6
recommendations.classNote: Against (recommends avoiding premature neuroprognostication)
recommendations.text: We recommend avoiding premature neuroprognostication in critically ill patients with AIS, including patients with severe ischemic stroke. While early neurological improvement (ENI) following revascularization may clarify a likely good outcome at 24 h, the appropriate period of observation in an individual patient should be determined with careful consideration of factors such as the anticipated evolution of neurological illness, potential confounders of the neurological exam, and completion of appropriate diagnostic imaging. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 7
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that critically ill patients with severe AIS, defined as NIHSS > 15, and/or their surrogates, be counseled that incremental functional recovery may occur up to 6 months, and sometimes longer, following the stroke, whereas most patients with AIS of mild to moderate severity will achieve the majority of their functional recovery within 3 months. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 8
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that critically ill patients with AIS who require artificial enteral nutrition, and/or their surrogates, be counseled that recovery of swallow function and removal of the feeding tube is likely, but not certain, within a period of several months among survivors. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 9
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that critically ill patients with AIS who require tracheostomy, and/or their surrogates, be counseled that successful decannulation is possible within a period of several months among survivors. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Good Practice Statement 10
recommendations.classNote: For
recommendations.text: We recommend that discussions of prognosis and goals of care for patients with large hemispheric infarction occur prior to neurological deterioration where feasible, to allow patients and surrogates sufficient time to make informed decisions on decompressive craniectomy and other therapeutic interventions. (Strong recommendation, evidence cannot be graded)

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 1: Age
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill adults with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest age alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 2: Admission NIHSS
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill adults with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest the admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 3: Hemorrhagic transformation
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest hemorrhagic transformation alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 4: Infarct size
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest infarct size alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 5: History of previous stroke
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling of critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest a history of previous stroke alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 6: Successful revascularization
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest successful revascularization alone not be considered a reliable predictor of good functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 7: Early neurological improvement
recommendations.classNote: For (the only predictor endorsed as moderately reliable)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest early neurological improvement (ENI) assessed 24 h following revascularization, or 24 h following admission for patients who are not candidates for revascularization, be considered a moderately reliable predictor of good functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later. A good outcome is expected in patients with recovery to an NIHSS of 0 to 1 at 24 h (weak recommendation; low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 8: Admission hyperglycemia
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest admission hyperglycemia alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical variables as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 9: Cerebral collateral circulation status
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the predictor NOT be relied upon) — as stated with the recommendation in Table 3; the GRADE evidence profile in Table 2 rates collateral status as Low
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest cerebral collateral circulation status alone not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical prediction models as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 10: ASTRAL score
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the model NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest the Acute Stroke Registry and Analysis of Lausanne (ASTRAL) score not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical prediction models as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 11: DRAGON, MR-DRAGON and MT-DRAGON scores
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the models NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest the Dense Artery, mRS, Age, Glucose, Onset-to-Treatment, and NIHSS (DRAGON), MR-DRAGON, and MT-DRAGON scores not be considered reliable predictors of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical prediction models as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 12: iScore
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the model NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest the Ischemic Stroke Predictive Risk Score (iScore) prediction model not be considered a reliable predictor of poor functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; very low quality evidence).

recommendations.section: Clinical prediction models as predictors of functional outcome — PICO 13: THRIVE, THRIVE-c and THRIVE-EVT scores
recommendations.classNote: Against (suggests the models NOT be relied upon)
recommendations.text: When counseling critically ill patients with AIS or their surrogates, we suggest the Totaled Health Risks in Vascular Events (THRIVE), THRIVE-c, and THRIVE-EVT scores not be considered reliable predictors of good functional outcome assessed at 3 months or later (weak recommendation; low quality evidence).
